stage_a.note: The pitch is upbeat and enthusiastic, with the founders modeling and dancing in the product.
Founders proudly display the rompers, speaking with high energy and animation.
Founders share friendly banter with each other, though mostly focused on presenting the product.

venture.description: A men's apparel brand selling fashionable rompers and jumpsuits.
venture.note: Founders state the ask clearly at the beginning of the pitch.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin introduces himself and states his hometown.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Wyatt introduces himself and states the ask of 200k for 5 percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin explains that men's clothing is boring and introduces the concept of the romper.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Wyatt introduces Romperjack as a brand for guys wanting to stand out and feel confident.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin highlights the variety of styles, points out the materials, and asks if Wyatt looks cool.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Wyatt thanks Justin, describes the romper as a self-esteem machine, and lists occasions to wear it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin invites the sharks to join them in this profitable opportunity.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Wyatt suggests they jump right into the numbers.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks about the valuation and requests their sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin states they have done 3.7 million dollars in sales over the last four years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter reacts positively to the sales figure.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori expresses impressed surprise at the sales numbers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks what their sales were in the last twelve months.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin answers that they did 1.1 million in the last year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks where and how they are selling the products.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin explains that they sell exclusively online through their own website.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond jokes that the romper is only for skinny guys and he would look pregnant in it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter asks who their target consumer is and who is buying the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin says their main consumers are gay men between 25 and 45, and also the college fraternity market.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they have any competition.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin admits multiple companies started in the space but claims they totally destroyed the competition.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Wyatt explains they saw a Kickstarter campaign for a male romper that wouldn't deliver until late summer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark jokes about the existence of a specific romper season.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Wyatt continues that they pulled money together and beat the Kickstarter campaign to market.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin challenges them, suggesting they basically knocked off someone else's idea.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Wyatt rejects the knockoff label, asserting that they simply did it better.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter asks Lori if she finds the founders attractive in their rompers from a female perspective.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori replies that the men are nice looking but she dislikes that the shorts match the top.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin states he understands the niche, noting his own investment in a similar space.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks Kevin why he is bringing up his underwear brand.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin explains that the shared community drives down customer acquisition costs through word of mouth.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks what the return rate is for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin answers that the return rate is about nine percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter asks how much they are selling the rompers for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin states the prices are around seventy-nine and sixty-nine dollars depending on the style.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin questions why the company is worth a four million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin justifies the valuation by detailing their steady revenue growth year over year up to 1.5 million projected.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they will generate any free cash flow on the projected revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin confirms they are cash flow positive and made 150k in profit the previous year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark congratulates them on being profitable.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they are paying themselves out of the profit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin confirms they are paying themselves.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks what their projected profit will be for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin predicts they will make between 300,000 and 350,000 dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if the two founders run the business by themselves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin states they run most of it, but hired stay-at-home moms for customer service.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark exits the deal, stating that clothing is simply not his area of interest.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Wyatt thanks Mark for his time.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond exits, explaining he cannot invest because he does not see himself wearing the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin thanks Daymond.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter exits, believing they will struggle to grow and he doesn't want to demand a large equity share.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin interrupts to present Romper Jill, an additional product line they forgot to mention.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks where Romper Jill is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin explains Romper Jill is a matching style they paused during covid but are bringing back.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori likes the matching idea but decides the business is not right for her and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin thanks Lori.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin notes he is the last shark, validates their sales, and expresses mixed feelings about the valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin tries to persuade Kevin by mentioning their inventory issues and high demand causing backorders.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin decides he does not love the product enough to invest and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Justin thanks the panel for their time.

decisions.note: Clothing is not his area of interest.
He cannot see himself wearing the style.
Believes they will struggle to grow and doesn't want to take a large equity chunk.
Does not feel it is the right business for her.
Likes the business but does not love it enough to invest.

record.notes: The pitch features high energy and modeling, though the investors ultimately decline due to a lack of personal interest or fit with the product style.
